title: Add explicit persistent conversation lifecycle

status.capability_ready: conversations provider ready after vault initialization

design.checkpoint: UI-35; backend lifecycle only, no visible UI change

ownership.independent_reviewer: pending; Lapo coordinates technical review and shared-file integration

behavior: Explicit create always allocates a new conversation; list/get/rename are bound to the server-owned workspace.
Open/closed status, order and active tab persist separately from canonical conversation history.
Close/reopen only changes metadata; no message deletion, stream dispatch or cancellation.
Stable timestamp-plus-ID cursors cover history and message pagination, including timestamp ties.
Legacy websocket channel reuse and latest-channel restoration remain operational; explicit chats have no channel.
Legacy list/message routes exclude foreign workspace rows and return 404 for unknown/foreign per-ID requests.
Authenticated lifecycle routes are supported but disabled unless JARVIS_BRIEF_CONVERSATIONS=1 at daemon startup.

acceptance.check: Two explicit conversations survive a database restart with independent messages and saved tab state
Unknown/foreign IDs are rejected; HTTP routes require panel authentication
Close/reopen preserves history and position; active-close fallback persists
Old clients restore the latest legacy channel conversation, including within the four-hour reuse window
Tied message timestamps paginate without gaps or duplicates
Fresh, upgraded and rolled-back old-writer databases preserve history and existing tab metadata

migration: Nullable workspace_id plus three metadata tables and two indexes. Existing message rows and old insert shapes remain valid. Legacy history receives closed tab metadata; old-writer rows acquire metadata on the next upgraded startup.
rollback: Remove the activation flag. Retain additive tables, IDs and history. Prior code can keep writing legacy conversations. Do not delete history, drop tables or replay effects.
limitations: Full repository F-02 CI has not run; validation is the targeted local suite and normal hooks.
No live daemon or user database was opened. No model, account, deployment or external effects were exercised.
The daemon remains one authenticated owner. Internal workspace scoping does not add multi-tenant identity/authentication.
History/reopen UI belongs to later dashboard work. F-03 transport and cancellation and F-04 client state are not implemented.
Messages retain the legacy shape without invented turn/request/event IDs.
The environment flag defaults off and has not been set on a running user daemon.
